best_for: Grad students and academics who write papers in Markdown, cite from Zotero, and want their notes kept as plain files on their own disk.
description:
Zettlr is a Markdown writing app for long academic work, from first notes to a journal submission or a book manuscript. Hendrik Erz started it in 2017, and it is developed between Sweden and Germany.

You decide how much formatting you see while you type, from plain code to near rich text, and LaTeX equations and Mermaid charts render in place so mistakes show up early. Export profiles hold a journal's template, so a paper comes out in the required format in one click, and other profiles build slides for Beamer, reveal.js or PowerPoint. Snippets with variables and tab stops insert boilerplate for you. You can also hook in LanguageTool for grammar checks and restyle the whole app with custom CSS.

points.title: Citations from your library
points.text: It reads references from Zotero, JabRef or Juris-M and formats them in any of more than 9,000 citation styles. Your bibliography is built as you write.

points.title: PDF export needs LaTeX
points.text: Exports run through Pandoc to Word, slides and more, but PDF output needs a LaTeX install with `xelatex` on your PATH. Plan for that download before a deadline.

points.title: A note system built in
points.text: Note IDs, wiki-style links between files and a graph view support a Zettelkasten way of working, so your reading notes and drafts can live side by side.

points.title: No cloud, no telemetry
points.text: Files stay on your computer and there is no forced sync. Zettlr says it collects no telemetry and only goes online to check for updates, which you can turn off.

points.title: Free, funded by donations
points.text: Zettlr is GPL-3.0 software with no paid tier and no account.

points.title: Where versions are kept
points.text: Windows installers come per-user or machine-wide (x64), and the Windows listing keeps 54 versions. macOS (Intel and Apple silicon, macOS 13 and later) and Linux list only the current release. The Linux Flatpak is verified for Zettlr, for x64 and Arm64.
